# Objective 3

## Objective

The aim of Objective 3 is to determine whether socioeconomic inequalities in smoking changed between 2014 and 2023.

This is assessed using multilevel modified Poisson regression models with interaction terms between each socioeconomic status indicator and survey year.

The key parameter of interest is: SES * survey year. 

This interaction tests whether the association between socioeconomic position and smoking differed in 2023 compared with 2014.

In this analysis:

- A ratio of prevalence ratios greater than 1 suggests that the socioeconomic inequality widened in 2023 compared with 2014.
- A ratio of prevalence ratios less than 1 suggests that the socioeconomic inequality narrowed in 2023 compared with 2014.
- A ratio close to 1 suggests little or no change in inequality over time.

All models include a random intercept for country and are weighted using the ESS analysis weight, `anweight`.

## 1. Load Packages and Prepare Data

This section loads the required packages and prepares the ESS dataset for multilevel modelling. Reference categories are set to ensure that model estimates compare each category with the intended reference group.

```{r load-packages-and-data}
# Load packages for data handling, modelling, model tidying, tables, and plots.

library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(broom.mixed)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)
library(gt)
library(ggeffects)

# Load the cleaned ESS dataset.
ess_clean <- readRDS("ess_clean.rds")

# Prepare the modelling dataset.
#
# Reference groups:
# - survey_year: 2014
# - sex: Male
# - marital: Married/Civil union
# - education: High
# - income_group: High
# - employment: Employed
# - occupation: Non-manual (higher)

ess_ml_data <- ess_clean %>%
  mutate(
    survey_year = factor(survey_year, levels = c("2014", "2023")),
    cntry = factor(cntry),
    
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    
    marital = factor(
      marital,
      levels = c(
        "Married/Civil union",
        "Never married",
        "Separated/Divorced",
        "Widowed"
      )
    ),
    
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c("High", "Medium", "Low")
    ),
    
    income_group = factor(
      income_group,
      levels = c("High", "Middle", "Low")
    ),
    
    employment = factor(
      employment,
      levels = c("Employed", "Inactive (other)", "Retired", "Unemployed")
    ),
    
    occupation = factor(
      occupation,
      levels = c("Non-manual (higher)", "Non-manual (lower)", "Manual")
    ),
    
    agea = as.numeric(agea)
  )

cat("Data loaded and prepared successfully.\n")
cat("Number of observations:", nrow(ess_ml_data), "\n")
cat("Number of countries:", n_distinct(ess_ml_data$cntry), "\n")
```


## 2. Define Outcomes and Socioeconomic Indicators

This section defines the smoking outcomes and socioeconomic status indicators used in the interaction models.

The smoking outcomes are:

1. Daily smoking  
2. Current smoking  
3. Ever smoking  
4. Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers  

The socioeconomic indicators are:

1. Education level  
2. Household income group  
3. Employment status  
4. Occupational class  

```{r define-outcomes-and-ses}
# Define smoking outcomes for Objective 3.
# The variable names correspond to the cleaned dataset.
# The labels are used in tables and plots.

obj3_outcomes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~outcome,           ~outcome_label,
  "Daily_smoker",     "Daily smoking",
  "current_smoking",  "Current smoking",
  "ever_smoking",     "Ever smoking",
  "daily_intensity",  "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers"
)

# Define socioeconomic indicators and their reference categories.

obj3_ses <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ses_var,       ~ses_label,                    ~reference,
  "education",    "Education level",             "High",
  "income_group", "Household income group",      "High",
  "employment",   "Employment status",           "Employed",
  "occupation",   "Occupational class",          "Non-manual (higher)"
)

# Check that all required variables exist in the dataset.

required_vars_obj3 <- unique(c(
  obj3_outcomes$outcome,
  obj3_ses$ses_var,
  "survey_year",
  "agea",
  "sex",
  "marital",
  "cntry",
  "anweight"
))

missing_vars_obj3 <- setdiff(required_vars_obj3, names(ess_ml_data))

if (length(missing_vars_obj3) > 0) {
  stop("Missing required variables: ", paste(missing_vars_obj3, collapse = ", "))
}

cat("Outcomes and SES indicators defined successfully.\n")
```

## 3. Interaction Models: Did Inequalities Change Over Time?

This section fits the primary Objective 3 models.

For each smoking outcome and each socioeconomic indicator, a multilevel modified Poisson regression model is fitted with an interaction between socioeconomic status and survey year.


The exponentiated interaction term is interpreted as a **ratio of prevalence ratios**. It indicates whether the prevalence ratio comparing a given SES category with its reference category changed in 2023 relative to 2014.

```{r interaction-model-function}
# This function fits one interaction model for one outcome and one SES indicator.

run_obj3_interaction_model <- function(data, outcome, outcome_label,
                                       ses_var, ses_label, reference) {
  
  model_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(.data[[ses_var]]),
      !is.na(agea),
      !is.na(sex),
      !is.na(marital),
      !is.na(survey_year),
      !is.na(cntry),
      !is.na(anweight)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      survey_year = factor(survey_year, levels = c("2014", "2023")),
      ses_exposure = factor(.data[[ses_var]]),
      ses_exposure = forcats::fct_relevel(ses_exposure, reference)
    )
  
  # Skip model if there is no variation in the outcome.
  if (nrow(model_data) == 0 || n_distinct(model_data[[outcome]]) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  model_formula <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ ses_exposure * survey_year + agea + sex + marital + (1 | cntry)"
    )
  )
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    glmmTMB(
      formula = model_formula,
      family  = poisson(link = "log"),
      weights = anweight,
      data    = model_data
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      message(
        "Interaction model failed for: ",
        outcome_label, " | ", ses_label, " | ",
        e$message
      )
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  broom.mixed::tidy(
    fit,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    conf.method = "wald",
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) %>%
    filter(str_detect(term, ":survey_year2023")) %>%
    mutate(
      Outcome = outcome_label,
      SES = ses_label,
      Reference = reference,
      Comparison = term %>%
        str_remove("^ses_exposure") %>%
        str_remove(":survey_year2023$"),
      ratio_of_PRs = estimate,
      CI_low = conf.low,
      CI_high = conf.high,
      p_value = p.value,
      Interpretation = case_when(
        p_value < 0.05 & ratio_of_PRs > 1 ~
          "Evidence that inequality increased",
        p_value < 0.05 & ratio_of_PRs < 1 ~
          "Evidence that inequality decreased",
        TRUE ~
          "No statistical evidence of change"
      ),
      n = nrow(model_data),
      countries = n_distinct(model_data$cntry)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Outcome,
      SES,
      Reference,
      Comparison,
      ratio_of_PRs,
      CI_low,
      CI_high,
      p_value,
      Interpretation,
      n,
      countries
    )
}
```


### Run Interaction Models

This chunk applies the interaction model function to every combination of smoking outcome and socioeconomic indicator.

```{r run-interaction-models}
cat("Running Objective 3 interaction models...\n\n")

obj3_interaction_results <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  obj3_outcomes,
  function(outcome, outcome_label) {
    
    purrr::pmap_dfr(
      obj3_ses,
      function(ses_var, ses_label, reference) {
        
        cat("Model:", outcome_label, "~", ses_label, "× survey year\n")
        
        run_obj3_interaction_model(
          data          = ess_ml_data,
          outcome       = outcome,
          outcome_label = outcome_label,
          ses_var       = ses_var,
          ses_label     = ses_label,
          reference     = reference
        )
      }
    )
  }
)

cat("\nInteraction models completed.\n")
cat("Number of interaction estimates:", nrow(obj3_interaction_results), "\n")

obj3_interaction_results
```


### Table 1: Interaction Results

This table presents the ratio of prevalence ratios for each interaction term.

A ratio of prevalence ratios above 1 indicates that the relative inequality was larger in 2023 than in 2014. A ratio below 1 indicates that the relative inequality was smaller in 2023 than in 2014.


```{r interaction-results-table}

obj3_interaction_table_clean <- obj3_interaction_results %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(
      Outcome,
      levels = c(
        "Daily smoking",
        "Current smoking",
        "Ever smoking",
        "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers"
      )
    ),
    SES = factor(
      SES,
      levels = c(
        "Education level",
        "Household income group",
        "Employment status",
        "Occupational class"
      )
    ),
    level_order = case_when(
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Medium" ~ 1,
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Low" ~ 2,
      
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Middle" ~ 1,
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Low" ~ 2,
      
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Inactive (other)" ~ 1,
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Retired" ~ 2,
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Unemployed" ~ 3,
      
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Non-manual (lower)" ~ 1,
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Manual" ~ 2,
      
      TRUE ~ 99
    ),
    `Ratio of PRs` = sprintf("%.2f", ratio_of_PRs),
    `95% CI` = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_high)
    ),
    `p-value` = case_when(
      is.na(p_value) ~ NA_character_,
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
    ),
    Comparison = paste0(Comparison, " vs ", Reference)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Outcome, SES, level_order) %>%
  select(
    Outcome,
    SES,
    Comparison,
    `Ratio of PRs`,
    `95% CI`,
    `p-value`
  ) %>%
  group_by(Outcome, SES) %>%
  mutate(
    SES = if_else(row_number() == 1, as.character(SES), "")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

obj3_interaction_table_clean %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Outcome") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table 1. Change in socioeconomic inequalities in smoking between 2014 and 2023**"),
    #subtitle = md("*Ratio of prevalence ratios from multilevel modified Poisson interaction models*")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    SES = "SES indicator",
    Comparison = "Level",
    `Ratio of PRs` = "Ratio of PRs",
    `95% CI` = "95% CI",
    `p-value` = "p-value"
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(SES, Comparison)
  ) %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(`Ratio of PRs`, `95% CI`, `p-value`)
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100),
    table.font.size = px(10),
    heading.title.font.size = px(15),
    heading.subtitle.font.size = px(12),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.background.color = "grey95",
    data_row.padding = px(2)
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    md(
      "*Ratio of PRs = ratio of prevalence ratios. Values greater than 1 indicate that the SES inequality was larger in 2023 than in 2014; values less than 1 indicate that the inequality was smaller in 2023 than in 2014. Models adjusted for age, sex, and marital status, included a random intercept for country, and were weighted using `anweight`.*"
    )
  )
```

### Forest plot of SES × survey year interaction effects

This plot visualises the ratio of prevalence ratios from the interaction models. It provides a graphical summary of whether socioeconomic inequalities in smoking widened or narrowed between 2014 and 2023.

 Interpretation:
- Ratio of PRs > 1: inequality was larger in 2023 than in 2014
- Ratio of PRs < 1: inequality was smaller in 2023 than in 2014
- 95% CI crossing 1: no statistical evidence of change

```{r forest_plot}


obj3_forest_data_clean <- obj3_interaction_results %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(
      Outcome,
      levels = c(
        "Daily smoking",
        "Current smoking",
        "Ever smoking",
        "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers"
      )
    ),
    
    SES = factor(
      SES,
      levels = c(
        "Education level",
        "Household income group",
        "Employment status",
        "Occupational class"
      )
    ),
    
    # Short SES labels for facet strips
    SES_short = recode(
      as.character(SES),
      "Education level" = "Education",
      "Household income group" = "Household income",
      "Employment status" = "Employment",
      "Occupational class" = "Occupation"
    ),
    
    SES_short = factor(
      SES_short,
      levels = c(
        "Education",
        "Household income",
        "Employment",
        "Occupation"
      )
    ),
    
    # Show only comparison category on y-axis
    Level_short = case_when(
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Medium" ~ "Medium",
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Low" ~ "Low",
      
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Middle" ~ "Middle",
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Low" ~ "Low",
      
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Inactive (other)" ~ "Inactive",
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Retired" ~ "Retired",
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Unemployed" ~ "Unemployed",
      
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Non-manual (lower)" ~ "Lower non-manual",
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Manual" ~ "Manual",
      
      TRUE ~ Comparison
    ),
    
    level_order = case_when(
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Medium" ~ 1,
      SES == "Education level" & Comparison == "Low" ~ 2,
      
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Middle" ~ 1,
      SES == "Household income group" & Comparison == "Low" ~ 2,
      
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Inactive (other)" ~ 1,
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Retired" ~ 2,
      SES == "Employment status" & Comparison == "Unemployed" ~ 3,
      
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Non-manual (lower)" ~ 1,
      SES == "Occupational class" & Comparison == "Manual" ~ 2,
      
      TRUE ~ 99
    ),
    
    change_direction = case_when(
      CI_low > 1 & ratio_of_PRs > 1 ~ "Increased inequality",
      CI_high < 1 & ratio_of_PRs < 1 ~ "Decreased inequality",
      TRUE ~ "No clear change"
    ),
    
    change_direction = factor(
      change_direction,
      levels = c(
        "Decreased inequality",
        "No clear change",
        "Increased inequality"
      )
    ),
    
    # Text label to show on the plot
    PR_label = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", ratio_of_PRs),
      " (",
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_low),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.2f", CI_high),
      ")"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Outcome, SES_short, level_order)

cat("Compact Objective 3 forest plot data prepared.\n")
```
```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
plot_obj3_outcome_forest_labeled <- function(outcome_name) {
  
  plot_data <- obj3_forest_data_clean %>%
    filter(Outcome == outcome_name) %>%
    mutate(
      Level_short = forcats::fct_reorder(Level_short, level_order, .desc = TRUE),
      
      outcome_title = case_when(
        outcome_name == "Daily smoking" ~ "Daily smoking",
        outcome_name == "Current smoking" ~ "Current smoking",
        outcome_name == "Ever smoking" ~ "Ever smoking",
        outcome_name == "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers" ~ 
          "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers",
        TRUE ~ outcome_name
      )
    )
  
  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = ratio_of_PRs,
      y = Level_short,
      colour = change_direction
    )
  ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 1,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.5,
      colour = "grey35"
    ) +
    geom_errorbarh(
      aes(
        xmin = CI_low,
        xmax = CI_high
      ),
      height = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) +
    
    # Add numerical ratio of PRs and CI label
    geom_text(
      aes(
        x = 1.83,
        label = PR_label
      ),
      colour = "black",
      size = 3.1,
      hjust = 0
    ) +
    
    facet_wrap(
      ~ SES_short,
      scales = "free_y",
      ncol = 1
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(
        "Decreased inequality" = "#2166AC",
        "No significant change" = "grey45",
        "Increased inequality" = "#B2182B"
      ),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    
    # Extend x-axis to leave room for text labels
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = c(0.75, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50, 1.75),
      limits = c(0.70, 2.20)
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = paste0("Change in socioeconomic inequalities between 2023 and 2014: ", plot_data$outcome_title[1]),
      subtitle = "Ratio of prevalence ratios from SES × survey year interaction models",
      x = "Ratio of prevalence ratios",
      y = NULL,
      colour = NULL,
      caption = paste0(
        "Values >1 indicate wider relative inequality in 2023 than in 2014; values <1 indicate narrower relative inequality.\n",
        "Reference categories: high education, high household income, employed, and higher non-manual occupation.\n",
        "Error bars show 95% confidence intervals; numbers show ratio of PRs (95% CI)."
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 14,
        hjust = 0
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 10.5,
        hjust = 0,
        margin = margin(b = 8)
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 10,
        hjust = 0
      ),
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey90",
        colour = NA
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        size = 9,
        colour = "grey15"
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        size = 9,
        colour = "grey15"
      ),
      axis.title.x = element_text(
        size = 10,
        margin = margin(t = 8)
      ),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
```

##Country-specific interaction model function

```{r}
run_obj3_country_interaction_model <- function(data, outcome, outcome_label,
                                               ses_var, ses_label, reference,
                                               country_value) {
  
  model_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      cntry == country_value,
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(.data[[ses_var]]),
      !is.na(agea),
      !is.na(sex),
      !is.na(marital),
      !is.na(survey_year),
      !is.na(anweight)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      survey_year = factor(survey_year, levels = c("2014", "2023")),
      ses_exposure = factor(.data[[ses_var]]),
      ses_exposure = forcats::fct_relevel(ses_exposure, reference)
    )
  
  # Skip model if there are too few observations
  if (nrow(model_data) < 100) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if outcome has no variation
  if (length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if only one survey year is present
  if (n_distinct(model_data$survey_year) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if SES variable has fewer than 2 categories
  if (n_distinct(model_data$ses_exposure) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  model_formula <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ ses_exposure * survey_year + agea + sex + marital"
    )
  )
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    glmmTMB(
      formula = model_formula,
      family  = poisson(link = "log"),
      weights = anweight,
      data    = model_data
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  broom.mixed::tidy(
    fit,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) %>%
    filter(str_detect(term, ":survey_year2023")) %>%
    mutate(
      Country = country_value,
      Outcome = outcome_label,
      SES = ses_label,
      Reference = reference,
      Comparison = term %>%
        str_remove("^ses_exposure") %>%
        str_remove(":survey_year2023$"),
      ratio_of_PRs = estimate,
      CI_low = conf.low,
      CI_high = conf.high,
      p_value = p.value,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Country,
      Outcome,
      SES,
      Reference,
      Comparison,
      ratio_of_PRs,
      CI_low,
      CI_high,
      p_value,
      n
    )
}

```

##Run country-specific interaction models

```{r}
countries_obj3 <- ess_ml_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(cntry)) %>%
  distinct(cntry) %>%
  pull(cntry)

obj3_country_interaction_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
  countries_obj3,
  function(country_value) {
    
    purrr::pmap_dfr(
      obj3_outcomes,
      function(outcome, outcome_label) {
        
        purrr::pmap_dfr(
          obj3_ses,
          function(ses_var, ses_label, reference) {
            
            run_obj3_country_interaction_model(
              data          = ess_ml_data,
              outcome       = outcome,
              outcome_label = outcome_label,
              ses_var       = ses_var,
              ses_label     = ses_label,
              reference     = reference,
              country_value = country_value
            )
          }
        )
      }
    )
  }
)

glimpse(obj3_country_interaction_results)

```

```{r}
obj3_country_interaction_results <- obj3_country_interaction_results %>%

        "Inequality increased",
      p_value < 0.05 & ratio_of_PRs < 1 ~ 
        "Inequality decreased",
      TRUE ~
```

Country-specific predicted prevalence model function


```{r}
run_obj3_country_predictions <- function(data, outcome, outcome_label,
                                         ses_var, ses_label, reference,
                                         country_value) {
  
  model_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      cntry == country_value,
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(.data[[ses_var]]),
      !is.na(agea),
      !is.na(sex),
      !is.na(marital),
      !is.na(survey_year),
      !is.na(anweight)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      survey_year = factor(survey_year, levels = c("2014", "2023")),
      ses_exposure = factor(.data[[ses_var]]),
      ses_exposure = forcats::fct_relevel(ses_exposure, reference)
    )
  
  # Skip model if too few observations
  if (nrow(model_data) < 100) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if outcome has no variation
  if (length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if only one survey year is present
  if (n_distinct(model_data$survey_year) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  # Skip model if SES variable has fewer than 2 categories
  if (n_distinct(model_data$ses_exposure) < 2) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  model_formula <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ ses_exposure * survey_year + agea + sex + marital"
    )
  )
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    glmmTMB(
      formula = model_formula,
      family  = poisson(link = "log"),
      weights = anweight,
      data    = model_data
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  pred <- tryCatch(
    ggeffects::ggpredict(
      fit,
      terms = c("ses_exposure", "survey_year"),
      type = "fixed"
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (is.null(pred)) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  as_tibble(pred) %>%
    mutate(
      Country = country_value,
      Outcome = outcome_label,
      SES = ses_label,
      Reference = reference,
      prevalence = predicted,
      CI_low = conf.low,
      CI_high = conf.high,
      prevalence_percent = prevalence * 100,
      CI_low_percent = CI_low * 100,
      CI_high_percent = CI_high * 100,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ) %>%
    rename(
      SES_category = x,
      Year = group
    ) %>%
    select(
      Country,
      Outcome,
      SES,
      SES_category,
      Reference,
      Year,
      prevalence,
      CI_low,
      CI_high,
      prevalence_percent,
      CI_low_percent,
      CI_high_percent,
      n
    )
}

```

Run country-specific predicted prevalence models
This runs the function across:

all countries,

all smoking outcomes,

all SES markers.

```{r}
obj3_country_predicted_prevalence <- purrr::map_dfr(
  countries_obj3,
  function(country_value) {
    
    purrr::pmap_dfr(
      obj3_outcomes,
      function(outcome, outcome_label) {
        
        purrr::pmap_dfr(
          obj3_ses,
          function(ses_var, ses_label, reference) {

              data          = ess_ml_data,
              outcome       = outcome,
              outcome_label = outcome_label,
              ses_var       = ses_var,
              ses_label     = ses_label,
              reference     = reference,
              country_value = country_value

    )
  }
)
```

Calculate change in inequality gap from 2014 to 2023

```{r}
obj3_country_change_absolute_inequality <- obj3_country_absolute_inequality %>%
  select(
    Country,
    Country_name,
    Outcome,
    SES,
    Reference,
    Comparison,
    Year,
    inequality_gap
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = inequality_gap,
    names_prefix = "gap_"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(gap_2014),
    !is.na(gap_2023)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    change_in_gap = gap_2023 - gap_2014,
    Direction = case_when(
      change_in_gap > 0 ~ "Widened",
      change_in_gap < 0 ~ "Narrowed",
      TRUE ~ "No change"
    )
  )

glimpse(obj3_country_change_absolute_inequality)
```

Make the clear descriptives-style plot
```{r}
plot_obj3_country_absolute_change_one_ses <- function(data, ses_name) {
  
  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(SES == ses_name) %>%
    mutate(
      Outcome_short = case_when(
        Outcome == "Daily smoking" ~ "Daily smoker",
        Outcome == "Current smoking" ~ "Current smoker",
        Outcome == "Ever smoking" ~ "Ever smoked",
        Outcome == "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers" ~ "Heavy daily smoking",
        TRUE ~ Outcome
      ),
      Direction = case_when(
        change_in_gap > 0 ~ "Widened",
        change_in_gap < 0 ~ "Narrowed",
        TRUE ~ "No change"
      ),
      Direction = factor(
        Direction,
        levels = c("Narrowed", "No change", "Widened")
      )
    )
  
  comparison_label <- plot_data %>%
    distinct(Comparison, Reference) %>%
    mutate(
      label = paste0(Comparison, " vs ", Reference)
    ) %>%
    pull(label) %>%
    unique() %>%
    paste(collapse = "; ")
  
  max_abs_change <- max(
    abs(plot_data$change_in_gap),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  
  x_limit <- ceiling(max_abs_change / 5) * 5
  
  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = change_in_gap,
      y = reorder(Country_name, change_in_gap),
      fill = Direction
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
      ~ Outcome_short,
      ncol = 2,
      scales = "free_y"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Narrowed" = "#2166AC",
        "No change" = "grey70",
        "Widened" = "#B2182B"
      ),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
      breaks = seq(-x_limit, x_limit, by = 10),
      labels = function(x) sprintf("%d", x)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        "Change in ",
        tolower(ses_name),
        " inequality in smoking, 2014-2023"
      ),
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Percentage-point change in the inequality gap by country: ",
        comparison_label
      ),
      x = "Change in inequality gap, percentage points",
      y = NULL,
      fill = NULL,
      caption = paste0(
        "Positive =widening inequality ",
        "Negative =indicate narrowing inequality. ",
        "Inequality gap = adjusted predicted prevalence in the comparison group-adjusted predicted prevalence in the reference group."
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 17
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 12.5,
        margin = margin(b = 12)
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 12
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9.5),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.x = element_text(
        size = 12,
        margin = margin(t = 8)
      ),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        colour = "grey88",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"),
      plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 8.5,
        hjust = 0,
        margin = margin(t = 10)
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 20, 20)
    )
}
```

```{r}
obj3_country_absolute_summary_table <- obj3_country_change_absolute_main %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome_short = case_when(
      Outcome == "Daily smoking" ~ "Daily smoker",
      Outcome == "Current smoking" ~ "Current smoker",
      Outcome == "Ever smoking" ~ "Ever smoked",
      Outcome == "Heavy daily smoking among daily smokers" ~ "Heavy daily smoking",
      TRUE ~ Outcome
    ),
    Direction = case_when(
      change_in_gap > 0 ~ "Widened",
      change_in_gap < 0 ~ "Narrowed",
      TRUE ~ "No change"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    SES,
    Outcome_short,
    Reference,
    Comparison
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    `Countries included` = n(),
    `Countries widened` = sum(Direction == "Widened", na.rm = TRUE),
    `Countries narrowed` = sum(Direction == "Narrowed", na.rm = TRUE),
    `Countries no change` = sum(Direction == "No change", na.rm = TRUE),
    `Median change, pp` = median(change_in_gap, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Largest widening country` = Country_name[which.max(change_in_gap)],
    `Largest widening, pp` = max(change_in_gap, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Largest narrowing country` = Country_name[which.min(change_in_gap)],
    `Largest narrowing, pp` = min(change_in_gap, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Median change, pp` = sprintf("%.1f", `Median change, pp`),
    `Largest widening, pp` = sprintf("%.1f", `Largest widening, pp`),
    `Largest narrowing, pp` = sprintf("%.1f", `Largest narrowing, pp`)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    SES,
    Outcome_short
  )
```
